reconcile.connective: JFB attribute the mismatch to when and where each register was drawn up — Ezra's list compiled in Babylon, Nehemiah's re-checked later in Judea.

discrepancy.connective: Steve Wells, in the Skeptic's Annotated Bible, presses the bare numbers: Ezra records 666, Nehemiah 667, and neither text explains or resolves the one-person gap.

skeptic.name: Steve Wells
skeptic.work: The Skeptic's Annotated Bible, "How many of Adonikam's offspring returned from Babylon?" (skepticsannotatedbible.com/contra/adonikam.html)
skeptic.attribution: Steve Wells, The Skeptic's Annotated Bible (online; contra/adonikam.html, attested by 2000)

excerpts.excerpt_text: But the discrepancy is sufficiently accounted for from the different circumstances in which the two registers were taken; that of Ezra having been made up at Babylon, while that of Nehemiah was drawn out in Judea, after the walls of Jerusalem had been rebuilt.
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: Directly names 'the discrepancy' between the Ezra 2 and Nehemiah 7 registers and gives the general reconciling mechanism (different time/place of compilation) that covers every mismatched family total, including Adonikam's 666 vs 667.

pd_work.resource: Keil & Delitzsch, Biblical Commentary on the Old Testament: Ezra, on Ezra 2:3ff.
pd_work.author: Keil & Delitzsch
pd_work.note: K&D set the Ezra 2 and Nehemiah 7 family totals side by side in a comparison table (including the Adonikam entry, 666/667) and attribute the surviving numeric differences across the lists to clerical/copying error rather than to an error in the original record. (Haley's 1874 Alleged Discrepancies could not be confirmed to treat this specific passage — no match for 'Adonikam' or 'Nehemiah vii. 18' in the full-text-searchable edition — so a row-surfaced harmonizing commentator keyed to the passage is used instead, per spec.)

link.title: CARM: Why are the statistics in Ezra 2 and Nehemiah 7 different?
link.note: Live apologetic treatment of the general Ezra 2 / Nehemiah 7 numeric mismatches (of which the Adonikam entry is one instance).
